question.text: Which of the following is NOT considered a financial asset?

answer.text: Equity shares of a listed company
Units of a mutual fund scheme

explanation.text: The Logic: A residential apartment owned directly is physical real estate, not a financial asset. Equity shares and bonds are financial assets held in paper or electronic form. The workbook distinguishes between financial form and physical form of assets, and notes that some asset classes such as real estate and commodities can be bought in either physical or financial form (for example, real estate held directly versus through REIT units, or gold held as jewellery/bars versus through gold ETFs). The Trap: Option C is the residential apartment held directly, which is the physical form of real estate. It is tempting to call it a financial asset because it generates rent or appreciates, but the classification depends on whether the holding is physical or in financial form, not on whether it earns returns. Note: Equity and bonds in this question are in financial form, while real estate and commodities can exist in either physical form (direct ownership) or financial form (units/ETFs). The residential apartment is the only option held purely in physical form.
